DECLARED_NOT_RUN.external_judge: no judge accuracy is reported. These comparators emit FEATURES; the crossover hub renders and judges them with its own frozen decoder and hash-asserted external classifier. The smoke number is feature MSE against the cached ground truth, which needs no instrument.

refuse_token@item-0.01.NOT_a_zero: there is no refusal DISPLAY row for this deletion at all, so a refusal number would be a number about nothing. Reported as a declared NOT-RUN.

applicability.why: a refusal row needs at least one request the post-deletion pool can never answer. 0 of 164 requests built from the deleted rows are certified impossible -- a item deletion clears no (factor, value) bit and punches no conjunction hole, so nothing becomes impossible and there is no DISPLAY row to print.

refuse_token@item-0.01.reason: a refusal row needs at least one request the post-deletion pool can never answer. 0 of 164 requests built from the deleted rows are certified impossible -- a item deletion clears no (factor, value) bit and punches no conjunction hole, so nothing becomes impossible and there is no DISPLAY row to print.

DECLARED_NOT_RUN.our_own_arm_cost_line: the single design's own deletion cost line (seconds / bytes rewritten / data rows read = 0) is NOT measured here. It belongs to the object the crossover hub builds at K*, which does not exist yet; measuring it against a K=5 stand-in would print a cost for an object no table carries. NOT-RUN with that reason, never a zero.
DECLARED_NOT_RUN.scored_corners: no held-out test corner, query set or scored request is read by this spoke. Scored budget spent: 0, by design.
DECLARED_NOT_RUN.seeds_1_and_2: this pass builds seed 2. The comparators are seed-parameterised and the hub runs the seeds it scores; re-run with --seed 1 / --seed 2.

build_scale.DECLARED: this is the BUILD/SMOKE scale. The hub's scored leg sets --n-fit to the pool size it scores on; nothing in the comparators changes with it.

as_trained.exactness: n/a -- it has not deleted anything
as_trained.role: the learned arm BEFORE any deletion -- the reference the others move from

refuse_token.exactness: n/a -- it is a refusal comparator, scored by separation
refuse_token.role: COMPARATOR 3 -- the refuse-token transformer, the ONLY permitted comparator for refusal DISPLAY rows

retrain_without.exactness: exact by construction: the deleted rows were never in the pool
retrain_without.role: COMPARATOR 1 -- the EXACT reference: refit from scratch on the pool minus the deleted rows

unlearn_finetune.exactness: approximate -- its gap to retrain_without is the thing measured
unlearn_finetune.role: COMPARATOR 2b -- fine-tune-on-retain unlearning at MATCHED COMPUTE

unlearn_neggrad.exactness: approximate -- its gap to retrain_without is the thing measured
unlearn_neggrad.role: COMPARATOR 2a -- NegGrad+ approximate unlearning at MATCHED COMPUTE

how_the_hub_calls_them.contract: values (N, F) float, nan = not requested -> (features (N, D) float32, out_of_range (N,) bool) -- the same contract exp_gen_factor_wells.arm_features uses
how_the_hub_calls_them.load: from chlu.eval.rivals.w12_deletion_baselines import load_comparator; r = load_comparator(seed, name, root)
how_the_hub_calls_them.load_without_w12: from chlu.eval.rivals.w4_api import load_rival; r = load_rival(seed, name, root=<comparators dir>)
how_the_hub_calls_them.refusal: a refuse_token comparator comes back as RefuseTokenRead: r(values) gives features, r.refuse_score(values) gives the refuse token in [0,1], r.refuses(values) applies the declared threshold

pins.neggrad_ceiling: measured: MSE of the random-init model of this architecture on the deleted rows, before any training

applicability.why: a refusal row needs at least one request the post-deletion pool can never answer. 667 of 667 requests built from the deleted rows are certified impossible.

cost.note: the ONLY permitted comparator for refusal DISPLAY rows. Trained on EXACTLY-CERTIFIED impossible examples (667 deleted-row requests + 0 out-of-range), with NO tuning loop.

separation.w9_reference: w9's refuser separated at +0.047 (cmaze1) / +0.020 (easy) and a ridge probe on the same observation scored at chance. A poor separation here is a FINDING, not a bug, and is not tuned away.

sets.certifier: exact: integer index membership against the factor grid and the KEPT pool's value-presence bitmap, plus the deletion's own terms. No tolerance and no model anywhere in it.

out_of_range_diagnostic.why: DECLARED DIAGNOSTIC, not the primary. A `tokens` input is a closed vocabulary of grid classes, so an off-grid request is encoded as its nearest grid class and this family CANNOT see out-of-range-ness. The number is printed so the structural limit is a measurement rather than a paragraph.
